targetText: The state is a product and a manifestation of the irreconcilability of class antagonisms. The state arises where, when and insofar as class antagonism objectively cannot be reconciled. And, conversely, the existence of the state proves that the class antagonisms are irreconcilable.
summary: Lenin restates the fundamental Marxist definition of the state as an organ of class rule arising solely because class conflicts cannot be peacefully harmonized within an exploitative society.

targetText: A standing army and police are the chief instruments of state power. But how can it be otherwise?
summary: Lenin points out that the material core of state power consists of armed forces and police separated from the mass of the people to maintain the rule of the property-owning minority.

targetText: the liberation of the oppressed class is impossible not only without a violent revolution, but also without the destruction of the apparatus of state power which was created by the ruling class
summary: Lenin clarifies that the working class cannot simply take hold of the existing capitalist state apparatus, but must smash and dismantle its repressive bureaucratic-military machinery.
